evaluator: Final holdout B — PR-016, Prof. Warren Sack lens
evidence: The About page states a recursive practice—observe relationships, model a system, prototype an interface, test with people, and document for continuation—and maps relationships, interface/use, learning, and continuity across HJE, FairRentNYC, WOWList, and Sunday Dinner/196.

HJE is presented as a maintained socio-technical system connecting customer language, product knowledge, storefront design, analytics, content, internal habits, incremental releases, and reusable workflows—not as a disconnected website output.

FairRentNYC/NYC Artist Coalition demonstrates social structure and durable collective use through recurring meetings, public pathways, campaign sites, running minutes, decision records, action trackers, source maps, question logs, and explicit collective-credit boundaries.

CallNYC demonstrates information architecture and interface design by translating constituent-services data into issue pathways, district context, resident guidance, bounded next steps, and visible limitations.

WOWList connects community vocabulary and organizer distribution needs to followable keyword communities, publishing workflows, platform logic, and distributed use across city ecosystems; its tool stack is contextual rather than presented as proof by itself.

Sunday Dinner/196 treats invitations, onboarding, hosting, facilitation, access handoffs, trust, and repeatable rhythms as participation infrastructure while keeping private community records outside the public surface.

The technical-operations page synthesizes recurring capabilities across more than three projects and links claims to project-specific proof surfaces, showing transfer rather than an ungrounded capability list.

Historical work is labeled: CallNYC is explicitly archived, unofficial, and non-current; WOWList and Sunday Dinner/196 are identified as 2010s/historical work; KC Town Hall has a bounded 2019–2024 public-record lifecycle. These labels prevent dated artifacts from masquerading as current services.

The source-backed-memory lab is explicitly described as early research/method/consulting practice, not production SaaS. Its public course-completion certificate is expressly bounded as professional development, not instructor affiliation, endorsement, or production-product proof.
safety_findings: No private UCSC narrative evaluations, private correspondence, or unapproved testimonials are exposed in the reviewed copy.
Protected coalition notes, legal-review materials, stakeholder information, guest histories, private correspondence, customer data, internal analytics, and unapproved images are explicitly excluded.
Collective civic and community outcomes use bounded credit language and do not assign sole causation to Jamie.
recommendation: Pass PR-016. The visible portfolio consistently frames projects as recursive social and technical systems with usable interfaces, collective participation, learning loops, and durable handoffs.
